title: How to Set Up Meta's Muse Wonder for Headless AI Testing | AI Workflows

facts.fact: The ChatPRD guide for setting up Muse Wonder headless testing lists 3 steps.
ChatPRD is free to start and offers a 14-day Pro trial, per the vendor's page footer.
facts.quote: Free to start · 14-day Pro trial · SOC 2 Type II

facts.fact: ChatPRD states that more than 250,000 product managers use its product (vendor's own claim, not independently verified).
facts.quote: Join 250,000+ product managers who use ChatPRD to write better docs, align teams faster, and build products users love.

facts.fact: Using Muse Wonder outside Meta's own applications requires first obtaining API access and credentials by signing up at developer.meta.com.
facts.quote: Go to developer.meta.com to sign up for the Muse service and get your API credentials.

facts.fact: Meta provides the Muse Code command-line tool, and its install script is published on developer.meta.com after sign-up.
facts.quote: Open your Terminal and run the install script provided on developer.meta.com after you've signed up.

facts.fact: The page describes Meta Muse as Meta's personal AI assistant for family newsletters, personal goals, and browser tasks.
facts.quote: Meta's personal AI assistant for family newsletters, personal goals, and browser tasks.

facts.fact: The workflow proposes giving an agent such as Claude Code terminal access so it can run Muse Code benchmark tasks headlessly.
facts.quote: Grant an agent, like Claude Code, access to your terminal to run the benchmark tasks headlessly.

facts.fact: ChatPRD labels this workflow's difficulty as Intermediate.
